page: Amazon Web Services c5n.metal is a bare-metal, compute-optimized server instance featuring 72 vCPUs and 36 physical cores powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8124M processors running at 3.4 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the system includes 192.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 2.67 GB of RAM per core. The hardware does not include local storage or GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 67384.33 and a PassMark CPU score of 50868.09, both placing in the top 25% tier. Memory read bandwidth is also strong, reaching 3741.32 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 212.97 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. However, single-core performance is average, as shown by a Geekbench single-core score of 1193.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1458.4.

The server exhibits a clear performance tradeoff in LLM inference tasks. While prompt processing speeds are average, text generation speeds are poor, falling into the bottom 10% with 6.09 tokens/sec for a medium 7B model due to the lack of hardware GPU acceleration. Given the 100 Gbps network bandwidth, strong multi-core processing, and strong database operations score of 22478.14 on PassMark, this instance is suited for network-bound compute workloads, multi-threaded applications, database operations, and high-throughput web serving.
